# Transmission Risk Map (portfolio demo)

A global, hierarchical transmission risk map for mosquito-borne diseases: malaria, dengue, Zika, chikungunya, yellow fever, West Nile fever and Japanese encephalitis.
**All risk values are synthetic**; they are generated by a seeded script, loosely following latitude so the map looks plausible. They are not real risk estimates.

## How it works

| Zoom    | Layer shown          | ID format    |
| ------- | -------------------- | ------------ |
| 0 – < 3 | Country (`adm0`)     | `KEN`        |
| 3 – < 6 | State (`adm1`)       | `KEN.12`     |
| 6 +     | District (`adm2`)    | `KEN.12.3`   |

- Each layer's Mapbox `minzoom`/`maxzoom` is a half-open range, so exactly one admin level renders at any zoom (`src/risk/zoomBands.ts`).
- A district with no value inherits its state's value. A state with no value inherits its country's value. A district whose state also has no value therefore shows the country's value (`src/risk/resolveRisk.ts`).
- Inherited values are drawn with a diagonal hatch over the risk colour. The info card names the area the value came from.
- Pick a disease from the header; the choice is kept in the URL (`?disease=dengue`).
- Hovering (or tapping) an area shows its risk in a tooltip at the pointer. Nothing shows off land.
- Pick a country in the header, or click one at country zoom, to zoom to it. Every area outside it is dimmed (`src/map/countryMask.ts`); pick "All countries" to go back to the world view.
- Map controls (zoom, locate, compass) sit top-left. One row under the page header holds the breadcrumb (left: separate pills for layer, disease and country; a bar along the bottom at 1000px and below) and separate Legend and Configuration buttons (right). Seas are drawn white (`src/map/baseStyle.ts`). The zoom level is centred at the bottom; the synthetic-data notice sits bottom-right. The page header names the author (`src/site.ts`). Its "Get a map like this" button links to `VITE_CONTACT_URL` and is hidden when that is unset.
- **Configuration** switches between transmission risk and elevation (Mapbox Terrain-RGB coloured by height), and toggles 3D terrain, hillshade and contour lines (Mapbox Terrain v2, from zoom 9) — `src/map/reliefLayers.ts`. In elevation mode the risk colours and hatching are hidden; admin outlines stay.
- The locate button under the zoom buttons zooms to your position. Hover or tap the blue dot for your area's risk level, resolved with the same fallback as the map (`src/data/locateUnit.ts`). Your position stays in the browser.

### Loading

| When                          | File                              | Size (gzip)            |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Start                         | `adm0.geojson`, `risk/{disease}.json` | ~130 KB + ~70 KB   |
| Right after the first view    | `adm1.geojson`                    | ~790 KB                |
| Zooming in past 4.5           | `adm2/{ISO}.geojson` for countries in view | 1 KB – 870 KB each (Brazil is the largest) |

## Run it

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env    # add a public Mapbox token (pk.*); optionally VITE_CONTACT_URL
npm run dev
```

- `npm test` runs unit tests for the inheritance, zoom-band, viewport, country-bounds and location lookup logic.
- `npm run build` runs the type checks and builds a production bundle into `dist/`.

## Deploy

Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which tests, builds and publishes to GitHub Pages at https://johnsaita.github.io/risk-map/.

- Add the Mapbox token as the repository secret `VITE_MAPBOX_TOKEN` (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions). Restrict the token to that URL in your Mapbox account, since it ends up in the public bundle.
- Optionally add `VITE_CONTACT_URL` as a repository variable.
- Set Settings → Pages → Source to "GitHub Actions".

## Data

`public/data/` is committed and can be regenerated:

```bash
npm run data   # download → simplify + assign IDs → generate synthetic risk
```

- `scripts/download-boundaries.ts` fetches geoBoundaries metadata and every openly licensed *simplified* country file into `data-raw/` (git-ignored, ~550 MB). It resumes if interrupted.
- `scripts/prepare-boundaries.ts` processes one country at a time:
  - simplifies each level with mapshaper, at a detail matched to its zoom band;
  - assigns hierarchical IDs; geoBoundaries ADM2 files don't reference their parent, so each district's state is found by a point-in-polygon test;
  - writes the files above plus `sources.json`.
- `scripts/generate-dummy-data.ts` writes one seeded `risk/{disease}.json` per disease. About 65% of states and 35% of districts get their own value; the rest inherit.

### Gaps in the source data

So that every zoom band covers every country:

- A country with no open national outline (India, Poland, Taiwan, Tuvalu, Puerto Rico) gets one built by merging its states or districts.
- A country with no states shows its national outline at state zoom.
- A country with no districts shows its states at district zoom. Those areas keep their state IDs, so they show the state's value.
- `sources.json` records which of these applied to each country.

### Boundary sources and licences

The boundaries come from [geoBoundaries](https://www.geoboundaries.org) (Runfola et al. 2020, *PLoS ONE* 15(4): e0231866). Each country file carries the licence of its upstream source, and `public/data/sources.json` lists the source and licence of every file used.

- **Allowed:** only openly licensed files are used: public domain/CC0/PDDL, CC BY, CC BY-SA, ODbL and national open-government licences. The allow-list is in `scripts/sources.ts`.
- **Excluded:** files under "Other – Direct Permission", "Other – Humanitarian", the Pixabay licence or Spain's INE licence. These were Poland and Taiwan ADM0, and Spain and Oman ADM2.
- **Share-alike:** ODbL (OpenStreetMap) and CC BY-SA sources require derived data to be shared under the same licence.

Base map © Mapbox © OpenStreetMap contributors.

Neighbouring countries' files come from different sources, so borders don't always line up. Disputed areas can also appear in more than one country.

## Structure

```
src/
  risk/        resolveRisk (fallback), zoomBands, levels (palette), diseases  + tests
  map/         addRiskLayers (sources, fill/hatch/outline layers), hatchPattern, countryMask, locationMarker, reliefLayers
  data/        boundaries (staged loading), risk (per disease), countriesInView, geometryBounds, locateUnit  + tests
  components/  SiteHeader, AboutDialog, RiskMap, Breadcrumb, CountryPicker, MapTools, LayersPanel, Legend, AreaInfo (pointer tooltip), ZoomBadge
scripts/       data pipeline
```
